title: Apply basic safety principles in the context of conservation

lessons.title: Dangers when working outdoors
lessons.html:
Dangers when working outdoors

Conservation work happens in the veld, along rivers, on dam walls and in nature areas. You may clear alien plants, fix fences, fight fires, build paths or stop erosion. The veld is beautiful, but it has dangers. Knowing them keeps you and your team safe.

Common dangers

DangerWhat to do
Sun and heatWear a hat and long sleeves. Drink water often. Rest in the shade.
SnakesWear boots. Look where you put your hands and feet. Never try to catch or kill a snake. Move away slowly.
Bees and waspsStay away from hives. If bees attack, run away and cover your face. Tell the team if you are allergic.
TicksCheck your body after work. Tell the clinic if you get a fever after a tick bite.
LightningStop work when a storm comes. Do not stand under a lone tree or on a hilltop.
Rivers and damsDo not cross a flooded river. Do not swim alone.
Wild animalsKeep away from buffalo, hippo, baboons and others. Never feed them.

Steep and rough ground

  • Walk, do not run, on slopes and rocks.
  • Look out for holes, loose stones and thorns.
  • Carry loads in a way that lets you see your feet.

Telling others

Never go into the veld alone without telling someone where you are going and when you will be back. Your team leader must know where everyone is. If you see a danger, warn your team straight away.

lessons.title: Using tools safely and dealing with emergencies
lessons.html:
Using tools safely and dealing with emergencies

Protective clothing (PPE)

  • Boots protect against thorns, snakes and dropped tools.
  • Gloves protect your hands when you pull alien plants or handle wire.
  • Safety glasses when cutting, chopping or spraying.
  • Hat and long sleeves against the sun.
  • Ear muffs when using a brush cutter or chainsaw.

Your employer must give you the PPE needed for the job. You must wear it and look after it. The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says both the employer and the worker have duties to keep the workplace safe.

Hand tools

  • Check the tool before use. A loose axe or panga head can fly off.
  • Keep blades sharp and covered when not in use.
  • Keep at least two arm lengths away from someone using a swinging tool.
  • Carry sharp tools with the blade pointing down.
  • Only use a chainsaw or brush cutter if you are trained and allowed to.

Herbicides

Some alien plant clearing uses herbicide. Only trained workers may mix and spray it. Follow the label. Wash your hands before eating.

In an emergency

  1. Stay calm and make the area safe. Do not put yourself in danger.
  2. Call your team leader. Know the emergency numbers and keep a charged phone or radio with the team.
  3. Give first aid only if you are trained. A first aid kit must be with the team.
  4. For a snake bite, keep the person still and calm, take off rings and tight things, and get them to a hospital fast. Do not cut the bite or suck it.
  5. For a veld fire, move away from the fire, upwind if you can, and warn others.

First aid needs hands-on training by an accredited provider. Ask your employer about a course.

Key points

  • Know the dangers: sun, snakes, bees, lightning, water and wild animals.
  • Always wear your PPE and look after it.
  • Check tools and keep a safe distance from swinging tools.
  • Never work alone without telling someone.
  • In an emergency, stay calm, make it safe and call for help.
